scope: Anonymous read of public freshness metadata. No local app/tests/browser or supplied credentials/cookies. Report statuses belong to server generatedAt; cached age is recorded. No cron/store refresh or production write invoked.

selectedDatasets.label: London pint-price dataset
selectedDatasets.cadence: episodic — re-collected by hand, then re-exported
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: manual (node scripts/refresh_pint_price_observations.mjs → python3 scripts/export_app_dataset_json.py --collected-at <ISO> --stamp-only → npm run canonicalize:venues → npm run build:slim). npm run export:data re-exports the committed CSV and re-collects nothing, and the bundled artifact carries layered rows the CSV does not hold, so it is not the collection step. See data/README.md.

selectedDatasets.label: Cheapest-pint baseline price updates (RETIRED)
selectedDatasets.cadence: none: a closed lane. No producer exists in this tree and none may be built against today's allowlist.
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: None. The hand-run publish (scripts/refresh_prices.mjs) and the parser module behind it (scripts/price_source_fetchers.mjs, whose fetchFromSource returned [] by construction) are DELETED rather than switched off, the refresh:prices package script is gone with them, and the nightly local-refresh scheduler no longer spends a slot on a command that could only ever write nothing. The registry used to name that command as this lane's refresh workflow, which read as progress somebody owed: it was not. The committed envelope stays EMPTY and its generatedAt dates NO observation: it is the day the empty envelope was aligned to the bundled pint dataset's own collection day, and it moves only when that day moves. Read it as an envelope date, never as a price date. This prose names no day of its own: the day the envelope is aligned to is whatever pint_prices reports, and a date typed here would rot the moment that one moved. Nothing restamps a row, because there are no rows.
selectedDatasets.gate: SUPPLY, not permission, and it is measured rather than assumed: on the 2026-09-03 re-read Greene King and Wetherspoon both PERMIT automated reading and publish no web pint price at all, while the one chain that does publish one (Nicholson's, Mitchells & Butlers) answers robots.txt with a Cloudflare 403 and is refused on permission. A first-party parser therefore has nothing permissible to parse, so data/price_sources.json `sources` now holds no source rather than two example-* placeholders. Reviving the lane is a captain SOURCE decision followed by a parser and a producer, never a budget or a cadence change. See lib/harvest/sourcePolicy.ts and docs/plans/CHAIN_PRICE_HARVEST.md.
selectedDatasets.detail: Retired: no producer for this lane exists in this tree, so no refresh is owed and none can be run. See refreshWorkflow and gate for what closed it.

selectedDatasets.label: Per-drink price updates
selectedDatasets.cadence: static snapshot: the rows describe the day they were collected and nothing may lawfully advance them
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: None. Captain ruling 2026-09-05: this lane is a static snapshot. The Drink price refresh workflow is retrieval-only and its ONLY permitted source (Wetherspoons) publishes no per-drink web prices, so no run can advance the file. A staleness budget here was a promise nobody could keep: the lane reported stale for ageing exactly as designed. Surfaces name it "Snapshot from <collection date>" (lib/dataFreshness.ts formatSnapshotFrom) and claim nothing about currency. Adding a source is a separate captain decision, not a budget change.
selectedDatasets.gate: Only allowlisted first-party source (Wetherspoons) has no per-drink web prices. Never restamp old rows after a zero-row retrieval.
selectedDatasets.detail: Aged 214.2h. A declared snapshot with no staleness budget: it reports the day it was collected, and no refresh is owed.

selectedDatasets.label: Food-menu price updates (RETIRED)
selectedDatasets.cadence: none: a closed lane. The 3 MB pack still ships and is still read; nothing writes it.
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: None, and `retired: true` is now what says so rather than a sentence a reader had to reach the end of. No script in this tree writes public/data/food_price_updates/latest.json: lib/priceUpdates.server.ts only reads it, scripts/firecrawl_greene_king_prices.mjs writes the DRINK pack beside it (its mapSectionToCategory returns null for every food section on purpose), and the Greene King rendered lane (scripts/harvest/uk-prices/render.mjs) writes the uk-prices overlay. `harvested by hand` was the last claim standing here and nobody harvests it: every row in the pack carries the same single import, which was never repeated. A 1440h budget was a promise nobody could keep before that: the lane reported stale for ageing exactly as designed and took the merge bar red with it (astra-review P0-1). The pack keeps serving and every row carries its own observedAt, which lib/priceUpdates.ts never presents as live. Writing a generator is a separate captain decision, not a budget or a status change.
selectedDatasets.gate: No writer, which is a stronger fact than a missing key: FIRECRAWL_API_KEY alone buys nothing while no script in the tree turns a permitted Greene King menu into a food row. The artifact is still opened by both freshness readers, so a pack that goes missing or stops parsing is still an UNRESOLVED breach: retiring a lane retires its refresh, never its file's integrity.
selectedDatasets.detail: Retired: no producer for this lane exists in this tree, so no refresh is owed and none can be run. See refreshWorkflow and gate for what closed it.

selectedDatasets.label: Night signals (offline-reviewed claims)
selectedDatasets.cadence: human-gated approved publish; no machine schedule
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: manual approved publish via npm run refresh:night-signals -- --open-pr; Vercel candidate ingestion never publishes reviewed claims
selectedDatasets.gate: Every claim passes human review before it ships, so this snapshot advances only on an approved publish. EXA_API_KEY arms the separate Vercel candidate-ingestion feed; it does not create a machine cadence for reviewed night_signals.

selectedDatasets.label: Night Signal candidate ingestion (Exa sweep, pending review)
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-night-signals sweeps Exa for dated, attributable London pub buzz and stamps feed_freshness (durable store, migration 0047 plane). Store-only, no committed artifact: /api/freshness and the freshness-audit cron both read the store's real observedAt directly (never a disk fallback, because none exists), and scripts/check_freshness.mjs queries the same table dependency-free. A store the checker cannot reach reports unmeasurable, never fresh and never stale. Hard staleness-budgeting an artifact-less cron feed is a registry-model follow-up. This feed reports when INGESTION last ran, not that any claim shipped.
selectedDatasets.gate: EXA_API_KEY (present in Vercel Preview + Production). Keyless = safe no-op. Candidates stay PENDING; durable candidate persistence and a store-based review surface remain follow-up work. Reviewed night_signals still advances only through an approved human publish.

selectedDatasets.label: Night-area weather cache
selectedDatasets.cadence: every 6h via Vercel cron (0 */6 * * * UTC); the durable weather_snapshots store is what the site reads and what this budget measures
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-weather → durable weather_snapshots store (read store-first via lib/weatherSnapshots.server). THE STORE IS WHAT IS MEASURED: a Vercel filesystem is read-only, so public/data/weather/latest.json can only age and a budget over it went red however healthy the cron was. That committed file stays as the degraded fallback and is dated by nothing. A runtime with no store credentials reports this feed unmeasurable: never fresh, never stale. GitHub Actions retired.
selectedDatasets.gate: none (Open-Meteo is keyless — the weather feed always runs)

selectedDatasets.label: What's-On (sport / quiz / deals / music / events)
selectedDatasets.cadence: twice-daily full What's-On refresh via Vercel cron (30 5 * * * and 0 15 * * * UTC); durable rows are preferred and bundled files remain the fallback
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-whats-on refreshes Ticketmaster/Skiddle events plus bounded quiz, deal, music, and sport lanes into the durable whats_on_listings store (read store-first via lib/whatsOnListings.server; bundled public/data/whats_on files are the fallback). GitHub workflows remain as a secondary recovery path when Actions billing returns.
selectedDatasets.gate: TICKETMASTER_API_KEY and/or SKIDDLE_API_KEY for official event rows (Skiddle also needs written commercial approval and SKIDDLE_BRAND_ASSET_PRESENT). The quiz lane is bounded to Question One pages; deal and music lanes use their existing first-party definitions and bundled venue inputs; the sport lane reads live fixtures (gate owned by whats_on_sport_fixtures). A failed lane leaves its prior durable rows unchanged. Live layer also blends CityMCP at request time.

selectedDatasets.label: What's-On sport fixtures (derived screenings)
selectedDatasets.cadence: twice daily via Vercel cron (05:30 and 15:00 UTC); bundled fixtures remain the offline fallback
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: Vercel cron GET /api/cron/refresh-whats-on fetches live fixtures (football-data.org football, TheSportsDB rugby) and re-derives sport rows into durable whats_on_listings; scripts/whatson/sportFixtures.mjs remains the local recovery path for the bundled fallback artifact
selectedDatasets.gate: FOOTBALL_DATA_API_KEY optional (the only football source; without it no football is listed and rugby still comes from TheSportsDB). THESPORTSDB_API_KEY required for rugby (paid key only; public test key 3 is never used). Past-dated rows are never served: lib/whatsOn.ts filterNotPast guards the serving seam.

selectedDatasets.label: London Pint Index (borough medians)
selectedDatasets.cadence: event-sourced — grows as confirmed Pint Drops / official-publisher observations arrive
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: user-cadence (the growth loop IS the refresh mechanism)
selectedDatasets.gate: none; only confirmed Pint Drops + official-publisher / open-data sources are eligible
selectedDatasets.detail: Aged 1841.1h, within the 2160h budget but over 30 days old: a snapshot of its collection day, not a current reading.

selectedDatasets.label: Area news (fresh-facts layer)
selectedDatasets.refreshWorkflow: manual (KEENABLE_API_KEY optional; npm run refresh:area-news, then node scripts/build_area_news_matches.mjs when venue badges need rebuilding)
selectedDatasets.gate: Keenable search_web_pages + fetch_page_content; a provider failure or zero valid facts leaves the prior dataset unchanged. Vercel cron cannot write this committed file, so refresh runs locally or in a review workflow.
